searchText: How you checked out the rust implementation of Enr? <https://github.com/sigp/enr/blob/master/src/lib.rs> Checking it right now. I see that their use a random seed when signing, I’m not yet sure how to replicate it in Zig. `sign_v4` uses OsRng but I'm not sure what OsRng does by default: https://github.com/sigp/enr/blob/master/src/keys/k256_key.rs#L33 https://docs.rs/signature/2.2.0/signature/trait.RandomizedDigestSigner.html#tymethod.try_sign_digest_with_rng Okay, so OsRng is a CSPRNG. I can create one in Zig, but need seed and if I use `std.posix.getrandom` I get a different signature each time (expected I guess, but then not sure why Rust library uses OsRng...). Anyways, I checked RLP again and it's correct. It's `[seq, k, v, ...]` just as the spec say. I supply the same private key as found in the spec and generate KeyPair (Zig exposes Signer through KeyPair). The public key in the KeyPair is same as in record's `secp256k1` field. So, RLP and keys are correct. I cannot understand why I keep getting different signature... I'm using Zig standard library to sign it (and verify - this part works): `std.crypto.sign.ecdsa.Ecdsa(secp256k1, keccak256)` -- I don't see anything fancy in ENR spec so I think the standard library should be able to do the job
